lines.text: Meanders: Meanders are loop-like bends present in the plains. Meanders become bigger because
of sluggish flow of water, and sometimes two bends of a meander may come close to each other
and form the neck of the meander. In case the river cuts through the neck of the meander to flow
straight,the cut-offloop becomes separatedandforms an ox-bow lake.
it deposits sand, sit, and clay. This deposition results in the formation of theflood plains overtime.
Levees:Ariverflow is fastest in the middle of theriver and its speed is slowest at the sides along
the river banks. This slow flowage of river water along its banks causes the dropping of much of the
sand, silt and clay by its sides. This dropped materialforms natural embankments called levees.
